q: The detailed classification of Government receipts, disbursements and other transactions, head by head, is contained in the publication known as the:

options.C: List of Major and Minor Heads of Account of Central and State Governments

e: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account of Central and State Governments contains the detailed head-by-head classification of receipts, disbursements and other transactions.

q: The Manual of Standing Orders (Audit), containing instructions for the conduct of audit work in the offices under him, is issued by:

options.B: The Finance Secretary to the Government of India
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The Manual of Standing Orders (Audit) is issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for audit work in offices under him.

q: The Contingency Fund of India was established under the:

options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.D: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003

e: The Contingency Fund of India was established under the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950, enacted under the constitutional provision for such a fund.

q: 'Voucher audit' in Government audit means audit conducted:

options.A: Only after the close of the financial year, with reference to the Appropriation Accounts
options.B: With reference to the vouchers and supporting documents evidencing each transaction, in order to see that the payment was duly authorised, correctly made and properly accounted for
options.C: At the residence of the disbursing officer, with reference to his personal accounts
options.D: By the internal audit wing of the Ministry, without reference to original vouchers

e: Voucher audit is audit with reference to vouchers and supporting documents to see that payment was duly authorised, correctly made and properly accounted for.

q: The statutory audit of expenditure on Indian Railways is, in its general character:

options.A: A pre-audit, in which no payment can be made until Audit has passed the bill
options.B: A concurrent audit, in which Audit sits with the executive at the time of every transaction
options.C: Mainly a post-audit, in which expenditure already incurred is audited afterwards with reference to sanctions, rules and vouchers
options.D: An audit dispensed with altogether, because Railways maintain commercial accounts

e: Railway expenditure is mainly post-audited by statutory audit: expenditure already incurred is checked afterwards against sanctions, rules and vouchers.

q: Under the standards of financial propriety, the splitting up of a purchase, a work or a sanction into smaller parts, merely in order to bring each part within the powers of a lower authority or to avoid the sanction of a higher authority, is:

options.A: Permitted, provided each part is separately accounted for
options.B: Permitted, provided the total value does not exceed the annual budget provision
options.C: Required, wherever the work is executed at more than one station
options.D: Not permissible; the requirement of sanction is determined by the total value of the transaction as a whole

e: Splitting a transaction to avoid higher sanction is impermissible; financial rules require sanction to be judged on the total value of the transaction as a whole.

q: A heavy rush of expenditure, particularly in the closing months of the financial year, is objectionable under the principles of Government financial control because:

options.A: It is regarded as a breach of financial propriety and sound budgetary control, and is liable to result in hasty, ill-considered and wasteful spending merely to avoid lapse of the grant
options.B: The accounts of the closing months are not audited by the C&AG
options.C: Expenditure incurred in March is automatically treated as unsanctioned expenditure
options.D: Grants voted by Parliament cannot legally be utilised in the last quarter of the year

e: A heavy rush of expenditure in closing months breaches financial propriety and budgetary control, as it leads to hasty and wasteful spending merely to avoid lapse of grant.

q: Adjustments in Government accounts which are not based on, and do not arise out of, actual transactions, but are made merely to utilise a grant or to present a desired figure, are known as:

options.B: Fictitious adjustments, and they are strictly prohibited in Government accounts
options.D: Book adjustments, and they require only the sanction of the Head of Office

e: Adjustments not arising from actual transactions, made only to utilise a grant or show a desired figure, are fictitious adjustments and are strictly prohibited.

q: The appearance of a minus (negative) balance under a suspense head in Government or Railway accounts ordinarily indicates that:

options.A: The head has been closed and requires no further action
options.B: A profit has been earned on the transactions booked under the head
options.C: The credits adjusted under the head exceed the debits, or debits and credits have been wrongly booked, so that the balance calls for investigation, correct linking and clearance
options.D: The balance has been written off with the sanction of the competent authority

e: A minus balance under a suspense head means credits exceed debits or entries are wrongly booked, so it calls for investigation, linking and clearance.

q: In the periodical review of suspense and remittance balances, 'unlinked items' are items which:

options.A: Have been outstanding for more than ten years
options.B: Have been accepted by Audit without objection
options.C: Relate to Railways other than the home Railway
options.D: Appear in one set of registers or returns but have not been linked and agreed with the corresponding entries in the other set of registers or in the general books

e: Unlinked items appear in one set of registers or returns but are not linked and agreed with corresponding entries in the other set or in the general books.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the balances of the State Provident Funds, such as the General Provident Fund of Government servants, are accounted for in the Public Account under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8009 in the Public Account is titled State Provident Funds, so balances of funds like the General Provident Fund are held under 8009.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 8009 from Major Head 8011 in the Public Account?

options.A: Major Head 8009 covers Insurance and Pension Funds, while Major Head 8011 covers State Provident Funds
options.B: Major Head 8009 covers State Provident Funds, while Major Head 8011 covers Insurance and Pension Funds
options.C: Major Head 8009 is operated in the Consolidated Fund, while Major Head 8011 is operated in the Public Account
options.D: Major Head 8009 covers the Provident Funds of Railway employees only, while Major Head 8011 covers those of all other Government servants

e: In the Public Account, 8009 covers State Provident Funds while 8011 covers Insurance and Pension Funds, as per their prescribed titles.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on pensions and other retirement benefits of Government servants is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2071 is titled Pensions and Other Retirement Benefits, so revenue expenditure on pensions and retirement benefits falls under 2071.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on miscellaneous general services, not covered by the specific general-services heads, is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2075, Miscellaneous General Services, is the residual head for miscellaneous general services not covered by specific general-services heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to the Council of Ministers is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2013 is the prescribed head for Council of Ministers, distinct from 2011 Parliament and 2012 President, Vice-President and Governor.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on the collection of taxes on income and expenditure is accounted for under Major Head:

options.B: 2020 - Collection of Taxes on Income and Expenditure
options.D: 2045 - Other Taxes and Duties on Commodities and Services

e: Major Head 2020 is titled Collection of Taxes on Income and Expenditure, so expenditure on such collection is classified under 2020.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on other fiscal services is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4046 - Capital Outlay on Currency, Coinage and Mint
options.C: 4047 - Capital Outlay on Other Fiscal Services

e: Major Head 4047 is the prescribed head for Capital Outlay on Other Fiscal Services in the 4-series capital heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans and advances given to Government servants, including house building advances, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 7610 is titled Loans to Government Servants and covers their loans and advances, including house building advances.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 4,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 3,050 crore, and appropriations of Rs 200 crore to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Rs 350 crore to the Pension Fund. Its Operating Ratio is:
e: Total working expenses are Rs 3,050 plus Rs 200 plus Rs 350 crore, that is Rs 3,600 crore. Operating Ratio is 3600 divided by 4000 times 100, that is 90 per cent.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic receipts of Rs 6,000 crore and total working expenses of Rs 5,100 crore. Its net revenue receipts are:
e: Net revenue receipts equal gross traffic receipts minus total working expenses: Rs 6,000 crore minus Rs 5,100 crore equals Rs 900 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a direct tax from an indirect tax, with reference to the impact and incidence of the tax?

options.A: In a direct tax, the impact falls on one person and the incidence on another, while in an indirect tax both fall on the same person
options.B: Direct taxes are collected by the Central Government only, while indirect taxes are collected by the State Governments only
options.C: In a direct tax, the impact and the incidence fall on the same person, who cannot shift the burden to another, while in an indirect tax the impact falls on one person and the incidence, after shifting, on another
options.D: There is no difference between the two, the distinction being only one of the rates charged

e: In a direct tax impact and incidence fall on the same person and cannot be shifted; in an indirect tax impact is on one person and incidence, after shifting, on another.

q: A tax is described as 'proportional' when:

options.A: The rate of tax increases as the tax base increases
options.B: The rate of tax decreases as the tax base increases
options.C: The amount of tax is fixed per unit of the commodity, irrespective of its value
options.D: The same rate of tax is applied at all levels of the tax base, so that the tax takes the same proportion of every tax base

e: A proportional tax applies the same rate at all levels of the base, so it takes the same proportion of every tax base.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'fee' from a 'tax'?

options.A: A fee is a payment for a specific service rendered to the payer, involving an element of quid pro quo, while a tax is a compulsory contribution to the common burden of the State, with no direct quid pro quo to the individual payer
options.B: A fee is collected only by the Central Government, while a tax is collected only by local bodies
options.C: A fee is always charged as a percentage of income, while a tax is always a fixed amount
options.D: There is no distinction, a fee being merely another name for a tax

e: A fee is payment for a specific service with quid pro quo to the payer, while a tax is a compulsory contribution to the common burden with no direct quid pro quo.

q: A 'special assessment', also called a betterment levy, in public finance is:

options.A: A tax levied at a special higher rate on luxury goods
options.B: A levy imposed on the owners of properties whose value has increased as a result of a public improvement, such as the construction of a road, in order to recover a part of the cost of that improvement
options.C: An additional assessment made by the audit authorities on detection of under-assessment of tax
options.D: A provisional assessment of tax made pending completion of the regular assessment

e: A special assessment or betterment levy is charged on property owners whose property value rose due to a public improvement, to recover part of its cost.

q: A 'single tax' system, in the classical public finance literature, means:

options.A: A system in which all taxpayers pay tax at a single uniform rate
options.B: A system in which tax is collected at a single point only, instead of at several points
options.C: A system in which the entire revenue of the State is raised from one single tax alone, as in the proposal to tax land values only
options.D: A system in which the Centre and the States levy one common tax in place of their separate taxes

e: A single tax system raises the entire State revenue from one tax alone, classically the proposal to tax land values only.

q: Under the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the preparation and submission of the accounts of a State to the Governor of that State, where those accounts are compiled by the C&AG, is provided for in:
e: Section 11 of the C and AG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for preparation and submission of State accounts compiled by the C and AG to the Governor.

q: On Indian Railways, 'internal audit', as distinct from the statutory audit of the C&AG, is carried out by:

options.A: The Accounts Department of the Railways itself, as an instrument of management for checking the efficiency and regularity of its own working
options.B: The Railway Board, through the Railway Protection Force
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General, through his resident audit parties
options.D: The Ministry of Finance, through the Controller General of Accounts

e: Railway internal audit is done by the Railways' own Accounts Department as a management tool, distinct from the C and AG's statutory external audit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India can be discussed in Parliament, but is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
2. No demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: charged expenditure under the Constitution can be discussed but is not voted, and no demand for a grant can be made except on the President's recommendation.

q: Under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, the total incremental guarantees extended by the Central Government in any financial year are capped at:

options.A: 5 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product
options.B: 2 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product
options.C: 1 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product
options.D: 0.5 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product

e: Under the FRBM framework, total incremental guarantees by the Central Government in a financial year are capped at 0.5 per cent of Gross Domestic Product.

q: The balances of subscribers to the General Provident Fund of Government servants form part of:

options.A: The Public Account of India, the Government holding the money in trust for the subscribers and being bound to repay it
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India, as a revenue receipt of the Government
options.D: The Block Account of the Railways

e: General Provident Fund balances are held in the Public Account of India, as government holds subscribers' money in trust and must repay it.

q: 'Escheat' as a source of Government revenue refers to:

options.A: Revenue realised from the sale of surplus Government stores
options.B: Property of a person who dies without any heir or legal claimant, which lapses to and is taken over by the State
options.C: Fees collected for the registration of documents
options.D: Interest earned on the investment of Government cash balances

e: Escheat is property of a person dying without heir or legal claimant which lapses to and is taken over by the State.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'double taxation' from 'multiple taxation'?

options.A: Double taxation means taxation at double the normal rate, while multiple taxation means taxation at more than double the rate
options.B: Double taxation is lawful in all cases, while multiple taxation is prohibited by the Constitution in all cases
options.C: Double taxation means the same person is taxed twice on the same income or subject by the same or two taxing authorities, while multiple taxation means a person or commodity is taxed at several points or by several authorities on different occasions, without the same charge being repeated on the identical base in the same period
options.D: There is no distinction, the two expressions being interchangeable in tax law

e: Double taxation taxes the same person twice on the same base in the same period, while multiple taxation taxes at several points or by several authorities without repeating the identical charge.

q: The results of the local audit and inspection of a Government office by the audit party are, in the first instance, communicated to the head of the office through a document known as the:
e: Local audit results are first communicated to the head of office through the Inspection Report issued by the audit party.

q: The Block Account of a Railway broadly shows:

options.A: The value of the assets of the Railway, classified according to the source from which they were financed, such as Capital, the Depreciation Reserve Fund, the Development Fund and Revenue
options.B: The day-to-day cash balance held at stations of the Railway
options.C: The balances outstanding under the traffic suspense heads of the Railway
options.D: The budget allotments made to the Railway under each Plan Head

e: The Railway Block Account shows the value of railway assets classified by source of finance, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund and Revenue.

q: The Combined Finance and Revenue Accounts of the Centre and the States, formerly compiled by the C&AG, ceased to be prepared in that form principally because:

options.A: The States refused to furnish their accounts to the C&AG
options.B: Following the separation of accounts from audit and departmentalisation of Union accounts, the Union Government began preparing its own Finance Accounts through the Controller General of Accounts organisation, and the States prepared their Finance Accounts through their Accountants General
options.C: The Finance Commission recommended the abolition of all Government accounts
options.D: Parliament directed that Government accounts be kept in a single combined volume

e: After separation of accounts from audit and departmentalisation, the Centre prepared Finance Accounts through the CGA and States through their Accountants General, ending the combined volume.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from land revenue are accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 0021 - Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax

e: Major Head 0029 is the prescribed receipt head for Land Revenue in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from stamps and registration fees are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 0030 is titled Stamps and Registration Fees, so receipts from stamps and registration fees are booked under 0030.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the interest receipts of the Government are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 0049 is specifically titled Interest Receipts, so government interest receipts are classified under 0049.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the dividends and profits received by the Government are accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 0071 - Contributions and Recoveries towards Pension and Other Retirement Benefits

e: Major Head 0050 is titled Dividends and Profits, distinct from 0049 Interest Receipts, so dividends and profits received fall under 0050.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to the President, Vice-President and Governor is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2012 is the prescribed head for President, Vice-President and Governor under General Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to stamps and registration fees is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 2020 - Collection of Taxes on Income and Expenditure

e: Major Head 2030 is titled Stamps and Registration Fees on the expenditure side, so such expenditure is classified under 2030.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to other taxes and duties on commodities and services is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2020 - Collection of Taxes on Income and Expenditure
options.C: 2045 - Other Taxes and Duties on Commodities and Services

e: Major Head 2045 is titled Other Taxes and Duties on Commodities and Services, covering expenditure relating to those taxes and duties.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to the Public Service Commission is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2051 is the prescribed head for Public Service Commission, distinct from 2052 Secretariat and 2053 District Administration.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to jails is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2056 is titled Jails, distinct from 2055 Police, so expenditure relating to jails falls under 2056.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on stationery and printing is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2058 is the prescribed revenue head for Stationery and Printing under General Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on family welfare is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2211 is titled Family Welfare, distinct from 2210 Medical and Public Health, so family welfare expenditure falls under 2211.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on water supply and sanitation is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2215 is the prescribed revenue head for Water Supply and Sanitation under Social Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on housing is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2216 is titled Housing, so revenue expenditure on housing is classified under 2216.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on social security and welfare is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2225 - Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Major Head 2235 is titled Social Security and Welfare, so revenue expenditure on social security and welfare falls under 2235.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on soil and water conservation is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2402 is titled Soil and Water Conservation, distinct from 2401 Crop Husbandry and 2403 Animal Husbandry, so such expenditure falls under 2402.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on fisheries is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Under the List of Major and Minor Heads, fisheries is a distinct function in the 240x agriculture and allied group, and Major Head 2405 is specifically assigned to Fisheries revenue expenditure.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on agricultural research and education is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2415 in the List of Major and Minor Heads is specifically assigned to Agricultural Research and Education, separate from crop husbandry, soil conservation and fisheries heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on rural employment is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2505 is specifically assigned to Rural Employment in the List of Major and Minor Heads, distinct from 2501 special programmes and 2515 other rural development programmes.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on shipping is accounted for under Major Head:
e: In the transport group, Major Head 3052 is specifically assigned to Shipping revenue expenditure, while 3051 is ports and light houses, 3053 civil aviation and 3054 roads and bridges.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on inland water transport is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3056 is specifically assigned to Inland Water Transport revenue expenditure in the List of Major and Minor Heads, distinct from shipping, road transport and other transport services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on atomic energy research is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3401 is specifically assigned to Atomic Energy Research, distinct from 3402 space research and 3425 other scientific research in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on census, surveys and statistics is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3454 is specifically assigned to Census, Surveys and Statistics in the general economic services group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on civil supplies is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3456 is specifically assigned to Civil Supplies in the List of Major and Minor Heads, distinct from census and statistics, tourism and secretariat economic services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on general economic services not covered by the specific economic-services heads is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3475 is the residuary head for Other General Economic Services, meant for economic services not covered by any specific major head in that group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on stationery and printing is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4058 - Capital Outlay on Stationery and Printing
options.C: 4046 - Capital Outlay on Currency, Coinage and Mint

e: Capital heads mirror the function with a 4xxx code: Major Head 4058 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Stationery and Printing in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on public works is accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 4058 - Capital Outlay on Stationery and Printing
options.D: 4047 - Capital Outlay on Other Fiscal Services

e: Major Head 4059 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Public Works, distinct from capital outlay on police, stationery and printing and other fiscal services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on family welfare is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4210 - Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health
options.B: 4215 - Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation

e: Major Head 4211 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Family Welfare, distinct from 4210 medical and public health, 4215 water supply and sanitation and 4216 housing.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on housing is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4215 - Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation
options.B: 4210 - Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health

e: Major Head 4216 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Housing in the social services capital group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on social services not covered by the specific social-services capital heads is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4250 - Capital Outlay on Other Social Services
options.B: 4225 - Capital Outlay on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities
options.C: 4235 - Capital Outlay on Social Security and Welfare

e: Major Head 4250 is the residuary head for Capital Outlay on Other Social Services, covering social services not assigned to a specific capital head.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on major irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 4711 - Capital Outlay on Flood Control Projects

e: Major Head 4700 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Major Irrigation, distinct from 4701 medium irrigation, 4702 minor irrigation and 4711 flood control projects.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on flood control projects is accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 4711 - Capital Outlay on Flood Control Projects

e: Major Head 4711 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Flood Control Projects in the irrigation capital group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on shipping is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5051 - Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses
options.C: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 5052 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Shipping, distinct from 5051 ports and light houses, 5053 civil aviation and 5054 roads and bridges.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on roads and bridges is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges
options.D: 5051 - Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses

e: Major Head 5054 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges in the transport capital group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on road transport is accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 5055 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Road Transport, distinct from the 5054 roads and bridges head which covers the road infrastructure itself.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans and advances given by the Central Government to the State Governments are accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 7601 - Loans and Advances to State Governments

e: Major Head 7601 is specifically assigned to Loans and Advances to State Governments in the loans group, distinct from loans to government servants and miscellaneous loans.

q: Civil Deposits which do not bear interest are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: In the Public Account, deposits not bearing interest fall in the 84xx series, and Major Head 8443 is Civil Deposits not bearing interest; 8336 is the interest-bearing counterpart.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the cheques and bills transactions are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8670 is specifically assigned to Cheques and Bills in the remittances group, covering cheques issued and bills transactions of government.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the departmental balances are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8671 is specifically assigned to Departmental Balances in the List of Major and Minor Heads, distinct from cheques and bills, cash balances and deposits with Reserve Bank.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the cash balances of the Government are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8673 is specifically assigned to Cash Balances, recording the cash balance of government, distinct from departmental balances and permanent cash imprest.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the deposits of the Government with the Reserve Bank are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8675 is specifically assigned to Deposits with Reserve Bank, recording government balances held with the Reserve Bank of India.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 0029 from Major Head 2029 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 0029 covers the receipts from land revenue, while Major Head 2029 covers the expenditure relating to land revenue
options.B: Major Head 0029 covers the expenditure relating to land revenue, while Major Head 2029 covers the receipts from land revenue
options.C: Major Head 0029 is operated in the Public Account of India, while Major Head 2029 is operated in the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Major Head 0029 covers the receipts from stamps and registration fees, while Major Head 2029 covers the receipts from land revenue

e: Receipt heads carry a 0xxx code and the corresponding expenditure heads a 2xxx code: 0029 is Land Revenue receipts and 2029 is Land Revenue expenditure, so option A states the distinction correctly.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 3054 from Major Head 5054 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 3054 covers the capital outlay on roads and bridges, while Major Head 5054 covers the revenue expenditure on roads and bridges
options.B: Major Head 3054 covers the revenue expenditure on roads and bridges, while Major Head 5054 covers the capital outlay on roads and bridges
options.C: Major Head 3054 covers the revenue expenditure on shipping, while Major Head 5054 covers the capital outlay on shipping
options.D: Major Head 3054 is operated only in the accounts of the State Governments, while Major Head 5054 is operated only in the accounts of the Union Government

e: The first digit distinguishes revenue from capital: 3054 is revenue expenditure on Roads and Bridges, while 5054 is Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges for the same function.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 8336 from Major Head 8443 in the Public Account of India?

options.A: Major Head 8336 covers Deposits of Local Funds, while Major Head 8443 covers Civil Deposits
options.B: Major Head 8336 covers Civil Deposits not bearing interest, while Major Head 8443 covers Civil Deposits bearing interest
options.C: Major Head 8336 covers Civil Deposits bearing interest, while Major Head 8443 covers Civil Deposits not bearing interest
options.D: Major Head 8336 is operated in the Consolidated Fund of India, while Major Head 8443 is operated in the Public Account of India

e: Civil Deposits bearing interest fall in the 83xx series under 8336, while Civil Deposits not bearing interest fall in the 84xx series under 8443, so option C is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on family welfare is accounted for under Major Head 2216.
2. In the same system, the revenue expenditure on housing is accounted for under Major Head 2211.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The heads are the reverse of those stated: family welfare revenue expenditure is under 2211 and housing under 2216, so both statements are wrong and the answer is neither.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the cheques and bills transactions are accounted for under Major Head 8670.
2. In the same system, the deposits of the Government with the Reserve Bank are accounted for under Major Head 8675.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct as per the List of Major and Minor Heads: cheques and bills are under 8670 and Deposits with Reserve Bank are under 8675.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from Union Excise Duties are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 0038 is specifically assigned to Union Excise Duties receipts in the tax revenue group, distinct from 0037 customs and 0020 corporation tax.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the interest payments of the Government are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2045 - Other Taxes and Duties on Commodities and Services

e: Major Head 2049 is specifically assigned to Interest Payments, covering interest on government debt, in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to treasury and accounts administration is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2054 is specifically assigned to Treasury and Accounts Administration, covering treasuries and the accounts and audit offices administration function.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on other administrative services, not covered by the specific administrative-services heads, is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2070 is the residuary head for Other Administrative Services, covering administrative services not assigned to a specific major head like police or district administration.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on technical education is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2203 is specifically assigned to Technical Education, distinct from 2202 general education and 2205 art and culture in the education group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on sports and youth services is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2204 is specifically assigned to Sports and Youth Services in the List of Major and Minor Heads, within the education, sports, art and culture sector.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on art and culture is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2205 is specifically assigned to Art and Culture, distinct from general education, technical education and sports and youth services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on dairy development is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2404 is specifically assigned to Dairy Development revenue expenditure, distinct from 2403 animal husbandry and 2405 fisheries in the agriculture and allied group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure relating to hill areas is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2551 is specifically assigned to Hill Areas revenue expenditure, covering special programmes for hill areas in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on medium irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2701 is specifically assigned to Medium Irrigation revenue expenditure, distinct from 2700 major irrigation, 2702 minor irrigation and 2711 flood control.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure relating to new and renewable energy is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2810 is specifically assigned to New and Renewable Energy revenue expenditure, distinct from 2801 power in the energy group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on industries other than village and small industries is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2852 is the general head for Industries, covering industries other than village and small industries under 2851 and non-ferrous mining under 2853.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on non-ferrous mining and metallurgical industries is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2853 is specifically assigned to Non-ferrous Mining and Metallurgical Industries in the industries group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on technical and economic co-operation with other countries is accounted for under Major Head:

options.B: 3605 - Technical and Economic Co-operation with Other Countries
options.C: 3604 - Compensation and Assignments to Local Bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions

e: Major Head 3605 is specifically assigned to Technical and Economic Co-operation with Other Countries, in the transfers group, distinct from grants-in-aid to State Governments under 3601.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on education, sports, art and culture is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4210 - Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health
options.C: 4202 - Capital Outlay on Education, Sports, Art and Culture
options.D: 4250 - Capital Outlay on Other Social Services

e: Major Head 4202 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Education, Sports, Art and Culture, mirroring the 220x revenue heads for that sector.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on information and publicity is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4250 - Capital Outlay on Other Social Services
options.C: 4235 - Capital Outlay on Social Security and Welfare
options.D: 4220 - Capital Outlay on Information and Publicity

e: Major Head 4220 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Information and Publicity in the social services capital group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on social security and welfare is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4235 - Capital Outlay on Social Security and Welfare
options.B: 4220 - Capital Outlay on Information and Publicity
options.C: 4225 - Capital Outlay on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities
options.D: 4202 - Capital Outlay on Education, Sports, Art and Culture

e: Major Head 4235 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Social Security and Welfare, distinct from 4225 welfare of SCs, STs, OBCs and minorities.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on crop husbandry is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 4401 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Crop Husbandry in the agriculture and allied capital group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on minor irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 4711 - Capital Outlay on Flood Control Projects

e: Major Head 4702 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Minor Irrigation, distinct from 4700 major and 4701 medium irrigation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on new and renewable energy is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 4810 - Capital Outlay on New and Renewable Energy

e: Major Head 4810 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on New and Renewable Energy, distinct from 4801 capital outlay on power projects.
